title: Protocol for absolute quantification of proteins in Gram-negative bacteria based on QconCAT-based labeled peptides
protocol: Grow the pre-culture of the selected Gram-negative bacterial strain for ∼16 h at its optimal growth condition in a 50-mL Falcon tube containing 10 mL of 2×YT medium.
Re-inoculate a 250-mL Erlenmeyer flask containing 50 mL of 2×YT medium by diluting the pre-culture 100× (500 μL).
Harvest 1 mL of the suspension by centrifugation at 10,000 g for 10 min at 4°C.
Remove the supernatant and freeze the cell pellets at -80°C until sample preparation.
Thaw the cell pellets on ice.
Add two 3-mm zirconium oxide beads to each sample.
Pipette 100 μL of lysis buffer into each sample.
Disrupt the cell suspension using a Mixer Mill set at 25 Hz for 5 minutes at approximately 20°C.
Heat the sample in a ThermoMixer at 99°C and 1,800 rpm for 10 minutes.
Centrifuge the sample at 15,000 g for 10 minutes at 23°C to remove cell debris.
Collect 50 μL of supernatant into a new Eppendorf tube.
Dilute the cell extract with 50 μL of 50 mM (NH4)HCO3.
Quantify protein concentration via the bicinchoninic acid assay.
Take 20 μg of protein for tryptic digestion into a new Eppendorf tube.
Dilute the tryptic digestion to reach a total volume of 100 μL using appropriate amounts of 50 mM (NH4)HCO3 solution.
Add 20 μL of 0.1 μg/μL trypsin and LysC digestion mix (ratio 1:1).
Initiate the tryptic digestion at constant shaking (400 rpm) for 8 hours and 37°C.
Add 10 μL of 10% (w/v) trifluoroacetic acid (TFA) to stop the tryptic digestion.
Vortex and centrifuge the samples at 15,000 g for 15 min at 23°C.
Perform StageTipping using C18 resin (solid phase extraction disk) to desalt the samples prior to HPLC-MS analysis.
Perform HPLC-MS analysis of the samples using a Dionex UltiMate 3000 coupled to an Orbitrap Exploris 480 operated with data-dependent acquisition.
Execute data analysis of the .RAW files using Proteome Discoverer.
Select peptides ranging from 350–5,000 Da in mass.
Avoid proline (P) residues on the carboxyl side of the cleavage site and acidic residues (D and E) on either side of the cleavage site.
Pick two or more proteotyptic peptides per protein with the highest fragment intensity.

Design pQconCAT vectors containing T7 RNA polymerase promoter region, ribosome binding site, quantification tag, sacrificial peptide, concatenated peptides, hexahistidine purification tag, STOP codon, antibiotic resistance determinant, and origin of vegetative replication (oriV).
Order the plasmid previously designed.
Transform competent E. coli BL21(DE3) ΔlysA ΔargH cells with pQconCAT vectors.
Grow a pre-culture of transformed E. coli in 5 mL of LB medium at 37°C for ∼16 h in a shaker at 250 rpm.
Inoculate 50 mL of fresh LB medium in a 250-mL Erlenmeyer flask with 0.5 mL of pre-culture to yield an OD600 ∼0.05.
Grow cells at 37°C in a shaker at 250 rpm until the culture reaches an OD600 ∼0.5 (∼2–3 h).
Transfer the cells to a pre-chilled 50-mL Falcon conical tube.
Harvest the cells in a pre-cooled centrifuge at 4°C for 10 min and 4,500 g.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in 1 mL chilled, filter-sterile 10% (v/v) glycerol solution and transfer to a chilled 1.5-mL Eppendorf tube.
Centrifuge for 1 min at 11,000 g and 4°C.
Discard supernatant.
Repeat washing steps at least twice.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 10% (v/v) glycerol to a volume of 500 μL relative to initial culture.
Transfer 30-50 μL aliquots to chilled 1.5-mL Eppendorf tubes.
Take competent cells E. coli BL21(DE3) ΔlysA ΔargH from -80°C and place them on ice.
Dilute the plasmid suspension in the tube to a concentration of 100 ng/μL using MQ water.
Add ∼25–50 ng of the plasmid into the cell tubes and vortex quickly one time.
Place cells and plasmid on ice for 30 min.
Incubate tube in water bath at 42°C for 60 s.
Return the cells to ice for 2 min.
Add 1 ml of LB medium (without antibiotics) to the tube containing the cells and plasmid.
Transfer the bacterial suspension into a 2-mL Eppendorf tube.
Incubate the bacterial suspension at 37°C in a Thermal Mixer with an 800 rpm shaker for 1 h.
Plate 50 μl of the cell suspension on LB agar plates (with the corresponding antibiotic) using pre-sterilized 2-mm glass beads.
Centrifuge the tube containing the remaining cells at 10,000 g for 5 min.
Discard most of the medium (∼900 μL).
Resuspend the cells in the remainder liquid.
Plate the cell suspension on LB agar plates (with the corresponding antibiotic) using 2-mm glass beads.
Incubate the plates for ∼16 h in an incubator at 37°C.
Pick the colonies, confirm presence of the plasmid by mini-prep and sequencing.
Prepare glycerol stocks of the selected clones.

Inoculate pre-cultures in 50-mL Falcon tubes containing 10 mL of M9 minimal medium with 40 mM glucose, 0.1 mg/mL U13C-L-lysine, and 0.1 mg/mL U13C-L-arginine + the selected antibiotic at 37°C at 200 rpm for ∼16 h.
Dilute pre-cultures 1:100 in 100 mL of M9 minimal medium and incubate in a 500-mL Erlenmeyer flask at 37°C until the culture reaches an OD600 of ∼0.5–0.6.
Cool down the flask to approximately 23°C.
Add IPTG to achieve a final concentration of 1 mM for expression induction and incubate at 30°C and 200 rpm for 24 h.
Centrifuge the culture at 3,000 g and 4°C for 20 min in a 250-mL Nalgene™ plastic bottle.
Freeze bacterial pellets at -20°C for 1 hour.
Thaw frozen pellets.
Resuspend biomass in 25 mL of resuspension buffer by vortexing.
Sonicate samples using a Vibra-Cell sonicator at 65% intensity for 10 minutes with ON-OFF cycles of 30 seconds, maintaining the samples at 4°C during sonication.
Incubate lysate with 2 μL of Pierce™ Universal Nuclease for Cell Lysis for at least 30 minutes at 23°C to digest DNA and reduce sample viscosity.
Centrifuge lysates for 20 minutes at 16,000 g in a cooled centrifuge (4°C).
Recover the pellet.
Resuspend the pellet in 2 mL of buffer A by pipetting up and down until the protein pellet is completely dissolved.
Centrifuge for 60 min at 4°C and 15,000 g.
Remove the supernatant.
Add 5–10 mL of buffer B to solubilize the protein, adding 1-mL aliquots at a time until the insoluble fraction is fully dissolved.
Stir gently for 1 h at 4°C in a waving shaker with an inclination of 30°C.
Centrifuge for 15 minutes at 4°C and 15,000 g to eliminate insoluble debris.
Store the supernatant containing the solubilized protein.
Assemble the purification Pierce™ Disposable Column by placing a filter disc in the bottom.
Cap the column tip and add 2 mL of HisPur™ Ni-NTA resin.
Mix the resin vigorously to form a homogeneous solution before adding it to the column.
Allow the resin to drain without becoming completely dry by removing the cap.
Recap the column once the resin is drained.
Place several 50-mL Falcon tubes under the column during different intermediate steps to collect fractions.
Add 2 mL of equilibration buffer and let the resin drain.
Cap the tip after adding the equilibration buffer.
Load the solution containing the QconCATs on top of the resin.
Collect the flow-through and repeat this step twice to increase protein recovery.
Keep the fraction containing the QconCATs at 4°C.
Wash the resin twice with 10 mL of equilibration buffer Ni-resin.
Elute twice with 2 mL of elution buffer.
Load the eluent in a 50-mL Amicon Ultra centrifugal filter (with a cut-off of at least 10 kDa below the size of the polypeptide of interest).
Proceed to exchange the buffer.
Centrifuge at 4,000–7,000 g for 10 minutes at 4°C.
Refill the column with 4 mL of sample exchange buffer.
Repeat centrifugation and refilling steps 3–4 times to properly exchange the buffer.
Pipette up and down to recover purified proteins in a final volume of 1 mL of the buffer.
Centrifuge the sample if more than 1 mL is obtained.
Measure protein concentration using NanoDrop 2000 spectrophotometer.
Mix components listed in Table 1 for protein samples in a 0.2-mL PCR tube.
Load ∼0.2–1 μg of purified protein in the polyacrylamide gel.
Incubate samples at 95°C for 5 minutes.
Spin down the samples in a spin microcentrifuge.
Take a Mini-PROTEAN TGX 4%–20% resolving gel.
Remove the comb carefully to avoid damaging the wells.
Insert the gel into a Mini-PROTEAN tetra cell vertical gel electrophoresis system.
Place the cell in the appropriate position of the tank buffer.
Use 1× SDS-PAGE buffer to fill the cell volume completely.
Fill the rest of the buffer tank up to the appropriate level mark.
Load 10 μL of the suspension sample.
Include at least one well with 2–3 μL of Page Ruler Plus Prestained Protein Ladder, 10–250 kDa.
Run the SDS-PAGE at 200 V for approximately 25 min.
Recycle the buffer outside the electrophoresis cell as long as the dye inside the precast cell has not escaped through the bottom of the gel.
Open the precast gel using a spatula or gel knife.
Wash the gel with distilled water.
Incubate the gel in ∼15–20 mL of Instant Blue staining with gentle shaking at 23°C.
Bands will be visible after 15 min and completely stained after 1 h.
Wash the gel to remove the dye by washing it with 30 mL of distilled water for 5 min.
Repeat this wash step three times.
Add 10 μL of each purified QconCAT from step 21.c.x to a new Eppendorf tube.
Add 60 μL of 0.1 μg/μL quantification tag peptide [Glu1]-fibrinopeptide B as internal standard.
Perform tryptic digestion.
Perform StageTipping.
Conduct HPLC-MS analysis.
Analyze data according to steps 6–14 of Section “peptide candidate mapping experiment”.
Determine the abundance of the spiked-in quantification tag (light peptide).
Determine the abundance of the 13C-labeled quantification tag from the QconCAT (heavy peptide).
Calculate the concentration of each QconCAT using Equation 1.
Perform cell lysis following steps 6–9 of Section “peptide candidate mapping experiment”.
Quantify total protein from the lysed cells.
Add an amount of each QconCAT protein corresponding to approximately the mass of endogenous proteins per 20 μg of total protein.
Digest samples with trypsin as described in steps 6–8 of Section “peptide candidate mapping experiment”.
Perform StageTipping on the digested peptides.
Inject the sample into HPLC-MS for separation and analysis.
Analyze data using Proteome Discoverer to determine peptide abundance.
